summary: Open-source data labeling tool for text, images, audio, video and time series, used to prepare training data and review model output.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Label Studio is an open-source data labeling tool. You set up projects with configurable labeling interfaces, import data from files or cloud storage, and label audio, text, images, HTML, video and time series, then export to model formats. It supports multiple users and projects, ready-made templates, a REST API and connections to ML models for pre-labeling.
sixtySeconds.problem: Training or fine-tuning models needs labeled data, and building a labeling UI for each data type is a lot of work. Label Studio gives you one flexible tool for all of them.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for broad data-type support, customizable interfaces, ML-assisted labeling and easy deployment with pip or Docker.

overview: Install with pip and run label-studio, or run the official Docker image with a local folder mounted for data. Either way it opens at localhost:8080. Docker Compose adds Nginx and PostgreSQL for production.
Create a project, pick a labeling template or write your own config, import data from files, S3 or Google Cloud Storage, and start labeling.
Connect an ML backend through the Label Studio ML SDK to pre-label data, retrain as you go or focus on hard examples. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
